title: Navimower 0.4.5-beta23

## Event-driven current-cycle checkpoints

Beta22 field diagnostics showed that the expensive filled mowing-area SVG could
take several seconds on large retained trails and was being rebuilt repeatedly
while the vendor geometry advanced. Beta23 separates the live view from the
retained base artifact.

- Keep polling and retaining the newest vendor trail geometry without rasterizing
  every geometry revision.
- During active mowing, use the already existing MQTT live tail as the moving
  presentation layer.
- Keep the last published per-zone SVG as a frozen same-cycle base.
- Anchor the live tail to the endpoint of that published base, not to the newest
  unrendered vendor geometry, so deliberately deferred builds cannot create a
  visible gap.
- Build a new expensive base only at lifecycle checkpoints:
  - integration startup for restored dirty vendor geometry;
  - leaving an active physical zone;
  - settling into docked / idle / charging / error after active work.
- Coalesce checkpoint requests while a render is already running and retain only
  the newest requested zone state.
- A confirmed ZoneLedger cycle/reset still revokes the old-cycle artifact
  immediately. Task membership and map revisions still do not reset trail truth.

The current Map Card protocol stays compatible: it continues to draw the
per-zone base artifact and MQTT live tail as separate layers.

## Artifact manifest semantics

- A same-cycle base remains usable while newer vendor geometry is waiting for
  its next checkpoint.
- `pending` now means that no usable base exists for the current cycle, rather
  than merely that vendor geometry is ahead of the published base.
- Add `geometry_ahead` and `artifact_geometry_revision` so diagnostics and
  future frontends can see that distinction without forcing a rebuild.
- Raw geometry updates no longer invalidate the prepared artifact cache key.

## Checkpoint diagnostics

`map_artifacts` diagnostics now expose:

- `mode: event_checkpoint_plus_mqtt_live_tail`;
- checkpoint count and per-zone build count;
- coalesced checkpoint requests;
- checkpoint failures, duration and trigger reason;
- dirty-zone count;
- checkpoint-building state.

This makes it possible to verify on H2/i1/X390 and larger trails that frequent
vendor observations no longer translate into frequent multi-second SVG builds.

## Truly static prepared-map identity

Beta22 removed two known georeference diagnostic branches, but field diagnostics
showed additional calibration/validation/refinement telemetry still caused
static resources to rebuild.

Beta23 hashes and serializes exactly the static presentation inputs:

- zones, Off-limit, VF-off, Channels, station, Gate Areas and Custom Areas;
- map identity/revision metadata;
- only the usable local-map -> WGS84 transform fields:
  reference point, rotation, source/status/model and map revision.

Calibration samples, validation report times, refinement diagnostics, candidate
diagnostics and other runtime telemetry no longer participate in static resource
identity.

A real polygon/map edit, Gate/Custom Area change or real georeference transform
change still publishes a new static resource.

## Unchanged truth semantics

No changes are made to:

- ZoneLedger cycle/reset arbitration;
- per-zone coverage/progress;
- the rule that scheduled-but-not-entered zones retain their previous trail and
  percentage until actual vendor evidence starts a new cycle;
- vendor geometry as the retained current-cycle authority;
- History/session archive ownership;
- mower commands or Schedule behavior.
